findings.problem: File I/O via fs::read_to_string fused into a function that returns a data structure, with unwrap() discarding the fallible Result
findings.failure_mode: untrusted path string causes a panic abort instead of returning a typed error; I/O side effects are hidden inside a function whose signature claims pure data loading
findings.fix: split into a shell function that reads the file and calls a pure parse_lines: &[str] -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError>, returning Result<Vec<Record>, FileReadError> at the boundary

findings.problem: unwrap() on fs::read_to_string Result discarding I/O failure
findings.failure_mode: missing file, permission error, or invalid path aborts the process instead of returning a typed error the caller can handle
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> and use map_err to convert io::Error into a domain-typed error

findings.problem: println! macro (stdout I/O) embedded in data-parsing logic
findings.failure_mode: pure domain logic leaks side effects to stdout; caller cannot suppress logging; output is not structured or traceable
findings.fix: move all I/O (println, fs reads) to the shell layer; parse function must be pure and side-effect-free

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(...).collect() allocates intermediate Vec and uses split instead of split_once for a two-field record
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary heap allocation per line; does not enforce field-count bounds; deviates from mandatory split_once pattern for one-separator grammars
findings.fix: use let (_name, value_str) = line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::Invalid)?; to parse exactly two fields without intermediate allocation

findings.problem: parts[0] unchecked indexing into a user-split Vec without bounds check
findings.failure_mode: empty line or malformed input with fewer than 1 field causes panic
findings.fix: use split_once and tuple destructuring; never index a split result directly

findings.problem: parts[1] unchecked indexing into a user-split Vec without bounds check
findings.failure_mode: line with only one comma-separated field causes panic at index 1
findings.fix: use split_once and tuple destructuring so second-field absence is a typed error, not a panic

findings.problem: unwrap() on parse::<u32>() discarding parse failure
findings.failure_mode: non-numeric value string (e.g., 'abc') causes a panic instead of returning a typed ParseError
findings.fix: use .map_err(|_| ParseError::Invalid) and propagate Result through the parse pipeline

findings.problem: Lossy as u16 cast on u32 parse result without checked conversion
findings.failure_mode: values in range 256..=4294967295 silently truncate to 0..65535, corrupting data without any error signal
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(|_| ParseError::Overflow) for a checked, lossless conversion

findings.problem: Record struct uses raw primitives (String, u16) for domain fields with no validation or type-level invariants
findings.failure_mode: any caller can construct Record with empty names, out-of-range values, or otherwise invalid data, violating make-illegal-states-unrepresentable
findings.fix: introduce newtype wrappers (e.g., Name(String) with smart constructor, or derive_from_str) and validate in a parse boundary function; use a typed error for construction failures

findings.problem: load_frames returns Vec<Record> with no error type; all failures manifest as panics
findings.failure_mode: missing file, empty file, malformed lines, parse failures, and overflow are indistinguishable at the call site; no graceful recovery path exists
findings.fix: define a ParseError enum with variants (Invalid, Overflow, TooMany, Allocation) and return Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError>

findings.problem: No bounded allocation strategy: no max_items cap, no try_reserve, no line-count limit
findings.failure_mode: an unbounded file with millions of lines causes OOM without any domain-level cap or graceful degradation
findings.fix: add a max_items domain cap to the function signature; validate input; call Vec::new() then values.try_reserve(max_items).map_err(|_| ParseError::Allocation)? before parsing; enforce per-line cap

findings.problem: I/O (fs::read_to_string), logging (println!), parsing (split/collect), type construction (Record), and conversion (parse/as) are all fused into a single 15-line function
findings.failure_mode: violates Data/Calculations/Actions architecture; no pure parsing function exists to test in isolation; hidden I/O in core logic
findings.fix: separate into: 1) shell fn load_frames(path) -> Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> that reads the file, 2) pure fn parse_lines(&[str], max_items) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> with bounded allocation, 3) move println to shell

findings.problem: No benchmark, profiler, or allocation evidence exists for the frame-loading path
findings.failure_mode: allocation behavior, throughput, and latency of load_frames are unmeasured; cannot verify whether intermediate Vec allocations or line-by-line parsing are optimal
findings.fix: add a benchmark measuring lines/second for representative input sizes; profile allocation hot paths; report baseline and verify optimization gains

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_frames throughput or allocation behavior
no profiler data for the file-reading and parsing hot path
no allocation budget or try_reserve evidence
no command-truth evidence (cargo fmt, cargo check, cargo clippy, cargo test were not run in review-only mode)
no second-ring evidence for any performance or correctness claims
residual_risk: This is a static-review-only assessment. No commands were executed. The source contains 8 BLOCKER-level violations spanning absolute law breaches (hidden I/O, unwrap, unchecked indexing, lossy cast, no typed errors, no split_once, no bounded allocation, raw-primitive domain types). The crate cannot be delivered without a full repair and verification pass.
